note: Daily runs take the first lesson whose day is not in state/history.json. Day N is planned for its 'date' at 10:00 IST. Keep the order beginner -> advanced.

lessons.title: What is Rust & why learn it
lessons.points: fast like C/C++, memory safe without a GC, great tooling (cargo), used by big companies

lessons.title: Install Rust & Hello, World!
lessons.points: rustup installs rustc+cargo; fn main; println! macro; rustc main.rs

lessons.title: Cargo: your Rust toolbox
lessons.points: cargo new, cargo build, cargo run, cargo check, Cargo.toml and target/

lessons.title: Variables & mutability
lessons.points: let is immutable by default; let mut; the 'cannot assign twice' error E0384

lessons.title: Constants & shadowing
lessons.points: const needs a type; shadowing with let x = x + 1 makes a new variable, can change type

lessons.title: Integers & floats
lessons.points: i32 is the default integer, u8..u128 / i8..i128, f64 default float, number literals 1_000

lessons.title: bool, char & integer overflow
lessons.points: bool; char is 4-byte Unicode; overflow panics in debug, wraps in release; checked_add / wrapping_add

lessons.title: Tuples & arrays
lessons.points: tuples (i32, f64) with .0 and destructuring; arrays [i32; 5]; out-of-bounds index panics

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.points: fn name(x: i32) -> i32; parameters need types; snake_case

lessons.title: Statements vs expressions
lessons.points: blocks are expressions; the last expression without ; is the value; why adding ; breaks a return

lessons.title: if / else
lessons.points: conditions must be bool; if is an expression: let x = if c { 1 } else { 2 };

lessons.title: loop & break with a value
lessons.points: loop { }; break value; returning a value from loop; continue

lessons.title: while, for & ranges
lessons.points: while; for x in collection; 0..5 vs 0..=5; .rev()

lessons.title: Loop labels
lessons.points: 'outer: loop { break 'outer; } to break out of nested loops

lessons.title: Comments & doc comments
lessons.points: // comments, /// doc comments, cargo doc --open

lessons.title: println! formatting
lessons.points: {} vs {:?}, inline {x}, width/alignment {:>5}, precision {:.2}, eprintln!

lessons.title: Ownership: the 3 rules
lessons.points: one owner per value; one owner at a time; value dropped when owner goes out of scope

lessons.title: Stack vs heap
lessons.points: fixed-size data on the stack; String's buffer on the heap; pointer, length, capacity

lessons.title: Move semantics
lessons.points: let s2 = s1 moves a String; using s1 after is error E0382

lessons.title: Copy vs Clone
lessons.points: integers/bool/char are Copy; .clone() makes a deep copy of a String

lessons.title: Ownership & functions
lessons.points: passing a String to a function moves it; returning gives ownership back

lessons.title: References & borrowing
lessons.points: &s borrows without taking ownership; the owner stays valid

lessons.title: Mutable references
lessons.points: &mut s; only one mutable reference at a time (E0499); no mixing & and &mut

lessons.title: No dangling references
lessons.points: the compiler rejects returning a reference to a local (E0106); return the owned value instead

lessons.title: Slices
lessons.points: &s[0..5], &str is a string slice, array slices &a[1..3]

lessons.title: String vs &str
lessons.points: String is owned and growable, &str is borrowed; String::from, .to_string(), &s as &str

lessons.title: Working with Strings
lessons.points: push_str, push, + and format!, why s[0] doesn't compile, .chars() and .bytes()

lessons.title: Structs
lessons.points: struct User { name: String, age: u32 }, field init shorthand, struct update syntax ..

lessons.title: Tuple structs & unit structs
lessons.points: struct Point(i32, i32); struct Marker; newtype idea

lessons.title: Methods with impl
lessons.points: impl Rect { fn area(&self) -> u32 }, &self vs &mut self vs self

lessons.title: Associated functions & new()
lessons.points: fn new(...) -> Self called as Type::new; multiple impl blocks

lessons.title: #[derive(Debug)] & dbg!
lessons.points: printing structs with {:?} and {:#?}; dbg! prints file, line and value

lessons.title: Enums
lessons.points: enum Direction { Up, Down }; variants with data: enum Message { Move { x: i32, y: i32 }, Write(String) }

lessons.title: Option: no more null
lessons.points: Option<T> is Some(T) or None; you must handle None

lessons.title: match
lessons.points: match must be exhaustive (E0004); arms bind values; _ catch-all

lessons.title: if let & let else
lessons.points: if let Some(x) = opt { }; let Some(x) = opt else { return; };

lessons.title: Pattern matching power moves
lessons.points: ranges 1..=5, | alternatives, match guards if x > 5, @ bindings, destructuring

lessons.title: Modules & pub
lessons.points: mod, privacy by default, pub fn, pub struct fields

lessons.title: use & paths
lessons.points: crate::, self::, super::, use to shorten paths, use ... as

lessons.title: Modules in files
lessons.points: mod foo; looks for foo.rs or foo/mod.rs; splitting a project

lessons.title: Vec<T>
lessons.points: Vec::new, vec![1, 2, 3], push, get returns Option, indexing can panic

lessons.title: Iterating & changing a Vec
lessons.points: for x in &v, for x in &mut v with *x += 1, why you can't push while borrowing

lessons.title: HashMap
lessons.points: use std::collections::HashMap; insert, get, iterate

lessons.title: HashMap entry API
lessons.points: entry(k).or_insert(0) and += 1 to count words

lessons.title: panic!
lessons.points: unrecoverable errors; RUST_BACKTRACE=1; panics on out-of-bounds

lessons.title: Result<T, E>
lessons.points: Ok and Err; matching on File::open; handling different error kinds

lessons.title: The ? operator
lessons.points: propagates errors early; works in functions returning Result or Option

lessons.title: unwrap & expect
lessons.points: unwrap panics on Err/None; expect adds a message; when it's fine to use them

lessons.title: main can return Result
lessons.points: fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> to use ? in main

lessons.title: Option combinators
lessons.points: map, and_then, unwrap_or, unwrap_or_default, ok_or

lessons.title: Custom error types
lessons.points: an error enum, impl Display, impl From<io::Error> so ? converts automatically

lessons.title: Generic functions
lessons.points: fn largest<T: PartialOrd>(list: &[T]) -> &T; zero-cost via monomorphization

lessons.title: Generic structs & enums
lessons.points: struct Point<T> { x: T, y: T }; Option<T> and Result<T, E> are generic enums

lessons.title: Traits
lessons.points: trait Summary { fn summarize(&self) -> String; } implemented for different types

lessons.title: Default trait methods
lessons.points: a default body in the trait; overriding it

lessons.title: Trait bounds & where
lessons.points: fn notify<T: Summary>(item: &T); multiple bounds with +; where clauses

lessons.title: impl Trait
lessons.points: fn f(x: &impl Summary) and returning impl Trait

lessons.title: Derive traits
lessons.points: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Default)]

lessons.title: Display trait
lessons.points: impl fmt::Display for your type so {} works

lessons.title: Operator overloading
lessons.points: impl Add for Point so p1 + p2 works

lessons.title: From & Into
lessons.points: impl From<i32> for Number; .into() comes for free

lessons.title: Lifetimes explained
lessons.points: 'a ties reference lifetimes: fn longest<'a>(x: &'a str, y: &'a str) -> &'a str

lessons.title: Lifetime elision
lessons.points: the three elision rules: why most functions need no 'a

lessons.title: Lifetimes in structs
lessons.points: struct Excerpt<'a> { part: &'a str } can't outlive what it borrows

lessons.title: 'static
lessons.points: string literals are &'static str; what 'static really means

lessons.title: Closures
lessons.points: |x| x + 1; type inference; capturing the environment

lessons.title: Fn, FnMut, FnOnce & move
lessons.points: how closures capture; move closures take ownership

lessons.title: Iterators
lessons.points: iter(), into_iter(), iter_mut(); iterators are lazy until consumed

lessons.title: map, filter, collect
lessons.points: chaining adapters; collect::<Vec<_>>()

lessons.title: Iterator power moves
lessons.points: enumerate, zip, take, skip, sum, fold, any, all

lessons.title: Implementing Iterator
lessons.points: impl Iterator for Counter { type Item; fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> }

lessons.title: Loops vs iterators performance
lessons.points: iterators compile to the same machine code: zero-cost abstractions

lessons.title: Box<T>
lessons.points: heap allocation; recursive types: enum List { Cons(i32, Box<List>), Nil }

lessons.title: Deref & deref coercion
lessons.points: * on Box; impl Deref; &String becomes &str automatically

lessons.title: Drop
lessons.points: drop runs when a value goes out of scope (RAII); std::mem::drop

lessons.title: Rc<T>
lessons.points: shared ownership; Rc::clone; Rc::strong_count; single-threaded only

lessons.title: RefCell<T>
lessons.points: interior mutability; borrow and borrow_mut checked at runtime; panics on violation

lessons.title: Rc<RefCell<T>>
lessons.points: multiple owners of mutable data

lessons.title: Weak & reference cycles
lessons.points: cycles leak with Rc; Weak<T> and upgrade()

lessons.title: Threads
lessons.points: std::thread::spawn and JoinHandle::join

lessons.title: move closures with threads
lessons.points: why threads need move; borrowing across threads is rejected

lessons.title: Channels
lessons.points: mpsc::channel, tx.send, rx.recv, multiple producers with tx.clone()

lessons.title: Mutex
lessons.points: Mutex::new, lock(), the guard unlocks on drop

lessons.title: Arc<Mutex<T>>
lessons.points: sharing a counter across threads; why Rc doesn't work there

lessons.title: Send & Sync
lessons.points: marker traits; the compiler prevents data races at compile time

lessons.title: Async/await basics
lessons.points: async fn returns a future; .await; futures are lazy

lessons.title: Trait objects: dyn Trait
lessons.points: Vec<Box<dyn Draw>>; dynamic vs static dispatch

lessons.title: Writing tests
lessons.points: #[test], assert_eq!, cargo test, #[cfg(test)] mod tests

lessons.title: Declarative macros
lessons.points: macro_rules!, how vec! works, repetition $( ),*

lessons.title: Capstone: what to build next
lessons.points: recap of the 90 days; project ideas: CLI tool (Book ch12), web server (ch21), contribute to open source
